issues.title: Resolve how the backend depends on sorokeep for verifyWebhookSignature
issues.scope: The published sorokeep@1.0.0 does not export verifyWebhookSignature. Verified by unpacking the tarball: dist/lib.d.ts exports only watchContract, runMonitorCycle, inspectContract, parseSacBalance, buildSacBalanceKeyXdr, formatTokenBalance and AWSSecretsResolver. The export exists only on the parent repo's main branch, added in commit 34148c8. Since FR-16 and the entire stated reason for a TypeScript backend rest on importing it natively, this must be resolved before E10 can compile. Reimplementing HMAC verification locally is explicitly the wrong answer — that is the mistake the TypeScript decision exists to avoid.
acceptance: Re-verify the published package before acting; it may have been republished since the audit. Run `npm view sorokeep version` and inspect the tarball's lib.d.ts, and paste both
Pick one path and record it: request a sorokeep release with a version bump, depend on the git ref until one exists, or vendor nothing and block E10
If depending on a git ref, the exact ref is pinned, not a branch name, and the ADR states the condition for switching to a published version
Whatever is chosen, prove it: install it in a scratch project and successfully import verifyWebhookSignature, pasting the output
The ADR names who owns getting a release published, since that is outside this repository's folder
nonGoals: Do not reimplement HMAC verification in this project under any circumstances.

issues.title: Scaffold the backend package with TypeScript and vitest
issues.scope: Create the backend package skeleton: package.json, tsconfig, vitest config, gitignore. No business logic. This is the container the rest of the backend epics fill.
acceptance: Node 22 or later is declared in engines, because sorokeep requires it
TypeScript is configured strict, with NodeNext module resolution — the provided port interfaces use .js extensions in their imports and will not resolve otherwise
vitest is the test framework, matching sorokeep's choice rather than introducing a second one
`npm install`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` all succeed on an empty project; paste the output
.gitignore excludes node_modules, dist and any local database file
`git status` confirms nothing outside lumens-vault/backend/ changed
nonGoals: No dependencies beyond what SCAFFOLD_BRIEF lists. No source files yet.

issues.title: Build the configuration module with fail-fast validation
issues.scope: The backend needs an RPC URL, network passphrase, contract id, database path, webhook secret, Reflector contract id and a port. None may be hardcoded and none may silently default to something wrong — a missing contract id that falls back to a placeholder produces an empty dashboard rather than an error, which is the worst failure mode.
acceptance: Every setting is read from the environment and validated at startup
A missing or malformed required value exits with a message naming the variable, rather than starting in a broken state
The contract id is validated for shape before use
The webhook secret is never logged, and a test asserts it does not appear in the config object's string representation
.env.example lists every variable with a comment, and no real value
Tests cover: all present, one missing, one malformed
nonGoals: No secret manager integration.

issues.title: Install the four port interfaces into the backend
issues.scope: The four interfaces staged by E01-05 are complete and type-check. Move them into place unchanged. They are the contract every adapter implements, so edits here ripple widely and should be separate, justified issues rather than incidental.
acceptance: All four files match the staged versions byte for byte; show a diff proving it
`npm run typecheck` passes with zero errors
The staging directory from E01-05 is removed
Any change deemed necessary is raised as its own issue rather than made here — state in the PR that none was made, or which issue was opened
nonGoals: No adapters yet.

issues.title: Design the SQLite schema for the display cache
issues.scope: The persistence port implies seven entities: cursor, events, vaults, whitelist, admin actions, sorokeep alerts and price cache. Design the tables before writing code, because getting amount storage wrong is expensive to discover later.
acceptance: Every table, column, type, primary key and index is specified
i128 amounts are stored as TEXT, never as a SQL numeric type or a JS number — state the precision-loss reasoning in the doc
The events table's primary key is the RPC event id, which is what makes ingestion idempotent
Each table maps explicitly to the port interface type it serves
States plainly that this database is a rebuildable cache: deleting it and re-ingesting must produce the same result, which is what NFR-4 allows
nonGoals: No Postgres or Redis; both are ruled out. Do not create tables that mirror Sorokeep's own.

issues.title: Implement the schema and a migration runner
issues.scope: Create the tables from E07-05 and a minimal, ordered migration mechanism so the schema can evolve without manual intervention on a developer's machine.
acceptance: Migrations are numbered, applied in order, and recorded so they run exactly once
Running the runner twice is a no-op; a test proves it
A test creates a fresh in-memory database, runs migrations, and asserts every expected table and index exists
The runner refuses to start against a database whose recorded version is ahead of the code, rather than corrupting it
nonGoals: No down-migrations; the cache is rebuildable.

issues.title: Implement event persistence with idempotent inserts
issues.scope: saveEvents must be idempotent by event id and return how many rows were genuinely new. Overlapping poll windows and retried requests will deliver the same event repeatedly, and double-counting a deposit would corrupt every derived balance.
acceptance: saveEvents inserts new events and ignores ones already present, returning the count actually inserted
A test saves the same batch twice and asserts the second call returns zero and the row count is unchanged
A test saves a batch containing both new and duplicate events and asserts only the new ones land
Amounts round-trip exactly as bigint through TEXT storage, including a value beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER — this is the assertion that catches a number conversion slipping in
nonGoals: No reorg handling; Stellar has immediate finality and rollback logic must not be built.

issues.title: Implement cursor persistence for ingestion progress
issues.scope: The cursor records how far ingestion has progressed. If it advances past events that were not durably stored, those events are lost silently — so the cursor and the events it covers must move together.
acceptance: getCursor and setCursor implement the port's IngestionCursor contract
getCursor returns null for a contract never ingested, and callers must handle that as a cold start rather than treating it as ledger zero
Cursors are keyed by contract id, so pointing the backend at a redeployed contract starts clean instead of resuming from a foreign position
A test asserts the cursor survives a reopened database connection
nonGoals: Polling logic is E08.

issues.title: Implement transactional writes across the repository
issues.scope: runInTransaction exists on the port because one ingestion step writes events, updates vaults and advances the cursor, and a crash between those leaves the cache inconsistent. Better-sqlite3 is synchronous, which makes this simpler than it looks, but the port exposes an async signature and the two must be reconciled deliberately.
acceptance: runInTransaction commits on success and rolls back on a thrown error
A test writes events and advances the cursor inside a transaction, throws partway, and asserts neither landed
How the synchronous driver is reconciled with the async port signature is explained in a comment, since the mismatch will confuse the next reader
Nesting behaviour is defined and tested, or explicitly rejected with a clear error
nonGoals: No connection pooling; SQLite with one process does not need it.

issues.title: Implement vault record persistence
issues.scope: The vaults table is the reconstructed read model the frontend's vault list reads. Upserts are keyed on user, asset and vault id together.
acceptance: upsertVault, getVault and getVaultsByUser implement the port contract
The composite key is enforced by the schema, so the same vault cannot be duplicated
Balances round-trip exactly as bigint
getVaultsByUser returns an empty array, never null, for an unknown user
A test covers a user holding vaults in several assets and asserts they all come back
nonGoals: Reconstruction logic is E09.

issues.title: Implement whitelist state persistence
issues.scope: The contract has no whitelist enumeration, so the current set is derived from Whitelist and Delist events and cached here. The deposit form's asset dropdown reads it.
acceptance: setWhitelisted and getWhitelist implement the port contract
An asset whitelisted, delisted and whitelisted again ends in the correct final state — assert the whole sequence, since last-write-wins is the property that matters
updatedLedger is stored so out-of-order processing can be detected
getWhitelist returns delisted assets with isWhitelisted false rather than omitting them, so the UI can distinguish delisted from never-listed
nonGoals: Derivation from events is E09-07.

issues.title: Implement admin action persistence
issues.scope: Admin actions are the only place pause, upgrade, whitelist changes and admin transfers are surfaced anywhere in the system — Sorokeep has no concept of them. Storage is keyed by event id so replays are idempotent.
acceptance: saveAdminAction and listAdminActions implement the port contract
Saving the same event id twice does not duplicate the row
listAdminActions returns newest first and honours its limit
Every AdminActionType from the port is storable and retrievable; a test covers all of them so a new action type cannot be silently unsupported
nonGoals: Detection is E09-08. Alerting is E09-09.

issues.title: Implement Sorokeep alert persistence
issues.scope: Verified webhook payloads are stored here and the Operations page reads them. The record shape mirrors Sorokeep's documented payload.
acceptance: saveSorokeepAlert and listSorokeepAlerts implement the port contract
Both documented alert types, threshold_crossed and alert_resolved, are storable, and a test pairs a crossing with its later resolution
listSorokeepAlerts filters by contract id and returns newest first
receivedAt is recorded separately from the payload's own timestamp, so clock differences between Sorokeep and this backend are visible rather than conflated
nonGoals: Signature verification is E10-08.

issues.title: Implement price cache persistence
issues.scope: Reflector readings are cached with an explicit status so the UI can distinguish a fresh price from a stale one, a deviant one, or none at all. The status is as important as the number.
acceptance: savePrice and getPrice implement the port contract
All four statuses round-trip: fresh, stale, deviant, unavailable
A reading may be null while the status is unavailable; a test covers that combination explicitly, since it is the case a naive implementation drops
Price values round-trip exactly as bigint alongside their decimals — a price is meaningless without its scale
nonGoals: Reflector integration and the guards are E11.

issues.title: Assemble the SQLite adapter behind the repository port
issues.scope: Compose the per-entity modules into one class implementing IVaultRepository, so the rest of the backend depends only on the port.
acceptance: The class implements every IVaultRepository method with no remaining stubs; typecheck proves completeness
It accepts a database path from configuration and supports an in-memory database for tests
Migrations run automatically on construction
An integration test exercises a realistic sequence — save events, upsert vaults, advance the cursor, read back — inside one transaction
No other module imports anything from adapters/sqlite/ directly; they import the port. State how this was checked
nonGoals: No second persistence implementation.

issues.title: Add structured logging
issues.scope: Ingestion runs unattended on a timer. Without structured logs, diagnosing why the dashboard is stale means guessing. The project that this one exists to showcase is a monitoring tool, so its own operability should not be an afterthought.
acceptance: Logs carry a level, a timestamp and a component field, and are JSON when not attached to a terminal
Log level is configurable and defaults to info
A test asserts the webhook secret and any configured key material never appear in output, even when the whole config object is logged
One example log line from each level appears in the PR
nonGoals: No external log shipping.

issues.title: Define the backend error taxonomy
issues.scope: Distinguish errors that mean the cache is temporarily behind — an RPC timeout, a rate limit — from errors that mean something is genuinely wrong, such as a schema mismatch or a failed signature check. NFR-4 tolerates the first class and makes them not worth alerting on; conflating the two produces either noise or silence.
acceptance: A small set of error classes distinguishes transient from permanent, with the retry policy stated for each
Every error carries enough context to identify what failed without reading the stack
Errors crossing the HTTP boundary map to sensible status codes and never leak internal detail to the client
The taxonomy is documented in a comment explaining the NFR-4 reasoning
nonGoals: No alerting; that is IAlertSink's job.

issues.title: Implement the alert sink port
issues.scope: IAlertSink is where this application's own alerts go: admin actions detected, price guards tripped, ingestion in trouble. It is deliberately not where Sorokeep's TTL alerts go — those arrive inbound via webhook. Start with a logging implementation; the port makes a real channel a later, isolated change.
acceptance: Implements IAlertSink and emits a structured log line per alert
All three alert kinds and all three severities are handled
The eventId field is used for idempotency where present, so a replayed event does not re-alert; a test proves it
A comment states that Sorokeep's alerts do not flow through this sink and explains why, since the two are easy to confuse
nonGoals: No Slack or email channel. No PagerDuty; explicitly out of scope.

issues.title: Bootstrap the HTTP server with health and readiness endpoints
issues.scope: The API process needs to start, bind a port and report whether it is actually working. Readiness is distinct from liveness here: the process can be alive while the database is unreachable or ingestion has fallen far behind.
acceptance: The server starts on the configured port and shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM, closing the database
A liveness endpoint returns 200 whenever the process is running
A readiness endpoint checks the database and reports ingestion lag, returning a non-200 with a body naming the failing dependency when unhealthy
Readiness reports how far behind the cursor is, since a backend that is up but hours behind is the realistic failure and NFR-4 makes it tolerable but worth surfacing
Tests cover both healthy and unhealthy responses
nonGoals: No business endpoints; those are E12.

issues.title: Write the backend README
issues.scope: A contributor picking up a backend issue needs to run it locally before they can do anything useful.
acceptance: Covers prerequisites, install, configuration, running in development, and running tests
Explains the hexagonal layout in a short paragraph: what belongs in domain, ports and adapters, and the rule that domain never imports an adapter
States plainly that this layer is a display cache and never the source of truth for fund safety, so a contributor does not over-engineer it
Every command was run and the output is in the PR
nonGoals: Not duplicating SYSTEM_DESIGN.

issues.title: Add an architecture boundary test
issues.scope: Hexagonal architecture holds only while the dependency direction does. A single import of the SQLite adapter from a domain module quietly destroys the testability the pattern was chosen for, and no reviewer catches that reliably.
acceptance: A test asserts no file under src/domain/ imports from src/adapters/
A test asserts domain modules import only from src/ports/ and standard libraries
The test fails when a violating import is added; demonstrate this by adding one temporarily and pasting the failure, then removing it
The failure message names the offending file and import
nonGoals: No general-purpose lint rule engine.

issues.title: Verify the backend scaffold against the scaffold brief
issues.scope: SCAFFOLD_BRIEF.md specified an exact tree. This epic built it incrementally across many issues rather than in one pass, so check the result against the brief and correct whichever is wrong — the brief is not automatically right, and at least one of its claims is known to need revision.
acceptance: The actual tree is compared to the brief's and every difference listed
Each difference is resolved in one direction with a stated reason: the code is corrected, or the brief is
The brief is updated to note that the four port files are provided pre-written rather than derived, which the addendum established but the brief never recorded
`npm install`, typecheck, lint, test and build all pass from a clean clone; paste the output
nonGoals: Frontend scaffold verification is E14-02.
